title: Lightly Row
short: Traditional (German folk song “Hänschen  · G 4/4 · listen, then play it.
trouble: Reading notes one at a time instead of in chunks.

blocks.html: This tune lives in G position: right thumb on the G above middle C, left little finger on the low G. The right hand uses only the five notes under its fingers. The first and last lines skip around the G chord (G, B, D); the middle lines move by step.
What to notice: German folk song from the first half of the 1800s, sung in English as “Lightly Row”

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys light up, and “wait for me” lets you practise one hand at a time.

items: the key of G major (key signature: one sharp)

blocks.html: Play through it once with the right hand only, then add the left. Which chord change made you stop?

sources.name: Melody checked note by note against the “Hänschen klein” page of the German Wikibooks songbook (LilyPond, in D major), moved up to G. English Wikipedia’s article on “Hänschen klein” says its melody is the tune of “Lightly Row”. The left hand is our own and follows that page’s chord symbols.
